They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"That again?" Willow sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Take your time."
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on that question."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."

"Elderberry — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"Chrysanthemum Greens — the root's the honest part. Dig a little and you'll know it anywhere."

"Still on whether they can trust you. Extremely normal, all of it."

"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." Every group I've been in, someone had to be the adult. Guess it's me again.
A laugh escapes them — short, surprised, real. The guard drops a notch.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Asher Franke is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Asher is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Stonebridge watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.
d41: 🕯️ Asher Franke is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Asher kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Asher's gone." Willow looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Asher." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Jasper blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Silver Tongue (Level 1). Words are tools. You've got a whole workshop.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Generous Heart (Level 1). Donating gives 2x trust.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Asher Franke, 41 days. The mantle passes to Jasper Rosales.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Jasper Rosales, 21 — a radio DJ. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Scream Cheese.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Asher — and Asher is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Willow, Sylvain, Victor and 4 more speak for Jasper — "Asher trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Jasper before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
